text: There is currently no direct evidence in PubMed supporting a specific pharmacological interaction between the ACE inhibitor Lisinopril and the cell cycle kinase CDK4 in the context of HR-positive breast cancer. Mechanistically, Lisinopril is a highly selective inhibitor of the angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) and is not known to possess off-target inhibitory activity against cyclin-dependent kinases. While the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) has been implicated in tumor microenvironment modulation, any potential link between Lisinopril and CDK4-driven proliferation would likely be indirect, involving systemic signaling pathways rather than direct molecular binding [PMID: 25603367]. Consequently, Lisinopril is not recognized as a therapeutic agent for targeting CDK4 in breast cancer oncology.
